Evince

/ih-VINS/ - rhymes with since · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Evince means to show or reveal clearly.

The old workbench itself evinces decades of careful habits: every tool outlined in paint, every drawer sliding without a squeak.

Worked Example

Buyers toured the orchard for an hour, and the ledgers evinced what the owner never said aloud: replanted rows after the blight, drainage dug in the wet years, a decade of patient spending on soil. The farm's history of care was legible in the numbers.

Evince means the evidence makes something inner or hidden plainly visible — attitudes, qualities, feelings. It is stronger than hint, but it stops short of prove: what is evinced is shown clearly, not demonstrated beyond argument.

How Evince Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

reveal

reveal: to bring anything hidden into view; evince is specifically evidence putting a quality on display

betray

betray: to reveal without meaning to — a tremor betrays nerves; evincing needn't be accidental

Antonyms

mask

mask: to cover a feeling so it cannot be read

hide

hide: the plain word for keeping something from view

How Strong Is It? — imply → evince → prove

imply vs. evince

imply vs. evince: To imply is to leave a trace for the alert reader; it stops well short of evince, which puts the quality on open display.

prove vs. evince

prove vs. evince: Prove goes further than imply on this ladder — proof settles the question beyond argument, while what is evinced is clearly shown yet still short of demonstrated.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — e-

Prefix — e-: out, thoroughly (Latin ex-)

Root — vinc

Root — vinc: to conquer (Latin vincere)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin evincere meant 'to conquer completely, to carry your point' — e- ('out, thoroughly') plus vincere ('to conquer'). In English the battlefield faded and the courtroom sense stayed: evidence that evinces a quality has won its argument on sight. The same vincere hides in convince, 'to conquer someone's doubts.'

Use the root in a new word: invincible

Use the root in a new word: invincible: With both champions injured, the team that had seemed invincible finally lost.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / written

Evince lives in reports, reviews and letters of reference: conduct evinces a quality. Use reveal for everyday showing, betray when the showing is accidental, and prove when the evidence settles the matter. People evince composure; documents evince care; nobody evinces a kitchen.
